label: Record type
definition: Editorial, erratum, note, thesis, chapter, preprint, abstract only
notes: Order 1; also by WoS DT and Scopus DOCTYPE

label: Language
definition: Non-English record
notes: Order 2; by language field, not by regex

label: Other platform
definition: Vehicle, aircraft, ship, legged or humanoid, exoskeleton, prosthesis, converter, drive, beam or generic plant without a manipulator model
include_regex: \b(quadrotor\w*|quadcopter\w*|uavs?|unmanned aerial|multirotor\w*|hexacopter\w*|aircraft|spacecraft attitude|satellite attitude|autonomous vehicle\w*|electric vehicle\w*|wheeled (mobile )?robot\w*|ships?|vessels?|auvs?|underwater vehicle\w*|legged|quadruped\w*|biped\w*|humanoid\w*|exoskeleton\w*|prosthe\w*|inverter\w*|power converter\w*|wind turbine\w*|euler[- ]bernoulli|simply supported beam)\b
notes: Order 3; EXCLUDE if include fires in title or >=2 times and exclude_regex fires only in the first or last sentence or not at all; otherwise UNCERTAIN

label: Multi-robot team level
definition: System-level FTC of multi-robot teams: formation, consensus, swarm, task reallocation among robots
notes: Order 4; EXCLUDE only if no actuator- or joint-level fault term; both fire -> UNCERTAIN (v1.2)

label: Fault out of scope
definition: Communication or network faults, cyber-attacks, software faults, collisions as faults, payload change
include_regex: \b(cyber[- ]?attack\w*|deception attack\w*|denial[- ]of[- ]service|dos attack\w*|false data injection|packet (loss|dropout)\w*|network(ed)? (fault|delay)\w*|communication (fault|failure|delay)\w*|collision detection|software fault\w*)\b
notes: Order 5; EXCLUDE only if no in-scope fault term

label: Diagnosis only
definition: Detection, diagnosis, isolation, estimation or prognosis without accommodation
notes: Order 6; v1.2: generic 'compensat', 'recover', 'redundan' no longer rescue a diagnosis record

label: Hardware design only
definition: Mechanism or hardware design with no control, switching or motion law
include_regex: \b(mechanism design|structural design|dual[- ]motor|redundant actuation design|joint module design)\b
notes: Order 7; low precision: both fire -> UNCERTAIN

label: Loss of effectiveness
definition: 0 < lambda_i < 1

label: Reduced torque bound
definition: Post-fault bound below nominal; nominal saturation alone is not a fault
notes: v1.2: generic 'saturation' removed (it is a constraint, coded as tag T-SAT below)

label: Stuck actuator or locked joint
definition: F4t stuck-at torque; F4q locked joint (sub-code at full text)

label: Free-swinging joint or total torque loss
definition: lambda_i = 0 and b_i = 0

label: Intermittent or time-varying fault
definition: Fault parameters switch or vary after onset

label: Transmission fault
definition: Motor-to-joint map changes
notes: v1.2: component words must be followed by a fault word

label: Sensor fault (secondary)
definition: Encoder, joint, velocity, torque or force sensor fault

label: Fault unspecified
definition: Actuator or joint fault named without a model
notes: Assigned when no F1-F8 fires

label: Time profile tag
definition: abrupt | incipient | intermittent | unspecified
notes: Tag

label: Active
definition: Fault detection or estimation feeding compensation or reconfiguration
notes: Evaluated before A1 Full-text note (stage E8-c2b, 25-11-2026; a reading of the v1.8 rule, not a rule change; the abstract rules of the mapping set are unchanged): a scheme is A2 when it computes online an estimate of the fault itself and that estimate enters the control law (the fault signal, a lumped term that the study states contains the fault, the effectiveness or its inverse, a bias or a stuck value), or when it detects or isolates the fault; it is A1 when it adapts only gains, bounds (including a bound on the fault magnitude or on the lumped term) or the weights of approximators of the fault-free dynamics, or adapts nothing.

label: Redundancy-based
definition: Kinematic or actuation redundancy
include_regex: \b(kinematic(ally)? redundan\w*|redundancy resolution|null[- ]space|redundant(ly)? (manipulator|robot|actuat)\w*|(torque|control) (re)?allocation|torque redistribut\w*|fault[- ]toleran\w* (workspace|configuration|motion planning|trajector|path planning)\w*|replann\w*|reduced[- ]order kinematic\w*)\b

label: Learning-based
definition: The accommodation itself is learned
notes: v1.2: bare 'policy' removed; neural approximators inside an adaptive law are T-ML, not A4

label: Passive
definition: Fixed robust or adaptive law without explicit fault information; mutually exclusive with A2 for one scheme (v1.8)
notes: v1.2: explicit term, or fallback when the record is FTC and neither A2, A3 nor A4 fires. v1.8: the fallback requires a named fixed robust or adaptive law (sliding mode, terminal sliding mode, super-twisting, adaptive, robust, backstepping, H-infinity, prescribed performance, passive fault tolerance; flag A1-LAW), otherwise A is unassigned (flag A-NR); A1 is dropped when A2 fires Full-text note (stage E8-c2b, 25-11-2026; a reading of the v1.8 rule, not a rule change; the abstract rules of the mapping set are unchanged): a scheme is A2 when it computes online an estimate of the fault itself and that estimate enters the control law (the fault signal, a lumped term that the study states contains the fault, the effectiveness or its inverse, a bias or a stuck value), or when it detects or isolates the fault; it is A1 when it adapts only gains, bounds (including a bound on the fault magnitude or on the lumped term) or the weights of approximators of the fault-free dynamics, or adapts nothing. Full-text note (stage E8-c3, 25-11-2026): the fault information used by a scheme is coded apart from the family in the extraction sheet (none; known, given a priori; obtained); A1 with known is a passive law with the fault given a priori.

label: Parallel
definition: Delta, Stewart, cable-driven parallel

label: Redundant serial
definition: Kinematically redundant serial arms

label: Space or free-floating
definition: Space manipulators

label: Collaborative, mobile, dual- or multi-arm
definition: One platform with joint- or actuator-level faults

label: Other
definition: Continuum and soft manipulators

label: Serial
definition: Serial arms, SCARA, industrial robots
notes: Explicit term, or fallback when no other M fires (flag M1-FALLBACK)

label: Physical manipulator (bin)
definition: Full physical manipulator with injected or real faults
notes: Abstract-based bin; full-text level assigned in L3

label: Bench or HIL (bin)
definition: Real actuator or joint rig, hardware-in-the-loop
notes: Checked before E4 only when no manipulator term accompanies the experiment

label: Simulation or analysis (bin)
definition: No hardware evidence in title, abstract or keywords
notes: Levels E0, E1, E2 are separated only at full text; E2 cues: simscape, gazebo, coppeliasim, mujoco, adams, co-simulation, pybullet, webots, robodk, isaac

label: Learning anywhere
definition: Learning or data-driven element in the pipeline

label: Digital twin
definition: Digital twin used

label: Input saturation considered
definition: Nominal actuator saturation in the design
notes: v1.2: replaces the generic part of F3

label: Open code or data
definition: Code or data stated as available

label: Benchmark or fault-injection protocol
definition: Named benchmark or explicit fault-injection protocol

label: Record by the author of the review
definition: Author list contains Urrea, C.
notes: Sensitivity analysis without OWN

label: FAME reporting checklist (L3)
definition: R1 equation; R2 magnitude; R3 onset and profile; R4 injection mechanism; R5 baselines; R6 metrics; R7 actuator limits; R8 noise or disturbances; R9 repetitions or statistics; R10 code or data
notes: Score 0-10
